items.title: Committed prebuilt binary extension module for CPython 3.6 Windows, unused by the code

findings.title: Committed prebuilt binary extension module for CPython 3.6 Windows, unused by the code
findings.explanation: A 99 KB compiled .pyd for CPython 3.6 win_amd64 is committed to the repository and installed with the extension (Auto3dgm/CMakeLists.txt installs the whole auto3dgm_nazar directory). Current Slicer releases use Python 3.9+, so the binary cannot load, and a search shows nothing in the extension imports lap_windows (only its own __init__.py/lapmod.py/tests reference it). Committed binaries of unverified provenance that are not needed should not ship; the upstream 'lap' package is the normal source.
findings.suggestion: Delete lap_windows (or exclude it from the install rule) and, if the solver is needed, depend on the upstream package installed on demand.

items.title: Long-running alignment runs synchronously on the GUI thread with no progress or error reporting

findings.title: Long-running alignment runs synchronously on the GUI thread with no progress or error reporting
findings.evidence:
def allStepsButtonOnLoad(self):
      self.Auto3dgmData.phase1SampledPoints = self.phase1PointNumber.value
      self.Auto3dgmData.phase2SampledPoints = self.phase2PointNumber.value
      Auto3dgmLogic.runAll(self.Auto3dgmData, self.reflectionCheckBox.checked)
      Auto3dgmLogic.exportData(self.Auto3dgmData, self.outputFolder, phases = [1, 2])
findings.explanation: runAll performs farthest-point subsampling plus an all-pairs Procrustes/assignment alignment (Correspondence computes n*n pairs, since has_pair at correspondence.py:128-135 always returns False) and mosek solves, all on the Qt main thread. Slicer freezes with no progress bar or cancel for the whole run, and failures surface only as tracebacks in the Python console rather than a dialog. The same applies to the individual step buttons.
findings.suggestion: Run the pipeline in a CLI module or a worker thread with slicer.util.progress / a progress dialog, and wrap failures in a user-visible error dialog.

items.title: No license terms for the Slicer module code itself

findings.title: No license terms for the Slicer module code itself
findings.evidence:
# Welcome to Slicer Auto3dgm!

For details please see our web page:

https://toothandclaw.github.io/
findings.explanation: The only license file in the repository is Auto3dgm/auto3dgm_nazar/LICENSE (MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2018 Julie Winchester et al.'), which covers the vendored auto3dgm_nazar package. There is no LICENSE at the repository root and the Readme states no terms, so distribution permission for the Slicer-specific code (Auto3dgm/Auto3dgm.py, meshviewer/) is not stated. The bundled three.js/jquery/OpenCTM assets do carry their own notices.
findings.suggestion: Add a root LICENSE (or explicit terms in the Readme) covering the Slicer module code, and keep the vendored MIT notice.

items.title: Unpinned pip_install('mosek') into Slicer's shared Python when the module widget is constructed

findings.title: Unpinned pip_install('mosek') into Slicer's shared Python when the module widget is constructed
findings.explanation: The install happens in Auto3dgmWidget.__init__, i.e. as soon as the module is opened, and installs an unpinned package into Slicer's shared Python environment, affecting every other extension in that Slicer installation. There is a confirmation dialog, which is why this is not blocking, but the dialog text also tells users to drop a license file into the installed extension's lib folder (wiped on extension update, and often not writable). The dependency is also proprietary (see license finding).
findings.suggestion: Pin a tested version, install only after an explicit user action (a dedicated button), and document the license path in a user-writable location instead of the install tree.

findings.title: Commercial/Academic dependency on MOSEK
findings.explanation: The extension requires the commercial optimization package MOSEK and an external license file to perform core correspondence analysis, which may limit out-of-the-box usability for community users without academic licenses.
findings.suggestion: Ensure users are well-informed about the MOSEK dependency and licensing requirements in the documentation.

findings.title: Mosek prompt continues module load when the user cancels, failing later
findings.explanation: If the user cancels the confirmation dialog, the widget constructor does nothing, and the module loads. Later, Correspondence imports mosek at the analysis step, which raises an unhandled ModuleNotFoundError in the GUI. The error is not reported to the user as a clear message.
findings.suggestion: Show an explicit error or disable the Run buttons when mosek is unavailable, and check the import before running an analysis step.

items.title: Visualize buttons clear the user's MRML scene without confirmation

findings.title: Visualize buttons clear the user's MRML scene without confirmation
findings.evidence:
def viewAlignedMeshWithinSlicer(viewMeshFolder, viewLmkFolder):
        slicer.mrmlScene.Clear(0)
findings.explanation: Clicking 'View Phase 1 alignment' or 'View Phase 2 alignment' (Auto3dgm.py:386-401) calls viewAlignedMeshWithinSlicer, which unconditionally clears the whole MRML scene. Any unsaved work in the user's current scene (loaded volumes, segmentations, markups, other module state) is discarded with no prompt and no undo. Fix: ask for confirmation, or load into a new scene / separate view without clearing.
findings.suggestion: Prompt with slicer.util.confirmOkCancelDisplay before clearing, or avoid clearing and only remove the nodes this module created.

items.title: meshviewer starts an unauthenticated HTTP server on all interfaces with unsanitized path handling

findings.title: meshviewer starts an unauthenticated HTTP server on all interfaces with unsanitized path handling
findings.explanation: serve_viewer() binds to ("", 8000), i.e. every network interface, and the overridden translate_path bypasses SimpleHTTPRequestHandler's '..' sanitization by plain string concatenation. Any host on the same network can therefore request e.g. /../../../../home/<user>/... and read any file the Slicer user can read, and the /mesh prefix serves the user's chosen mesh directory (their research/medical surface data) with no authentication. Reachable when a user launches the installed 'meshviewer' CLI module (meshviewer/meshviewer.py -> web_view_mesh.viewer.serve_viewer); the Auto3dgm module's own server button is commented out, which limits but does not remove the exposure. Fix: bind to 127.0.0.1 and normalize/validate the resolved path against the allowed roots.
findings.suggestion: Bind to ('127.0.0.1', port) and resolve paths with os.path.realpath + a commonpath check against the allowed directories before serving.

findings.title: Mesh viewer HTTP server binds to all interfaces and allows path traversal outside the mesh folder
findings.explanation: serve_viewer starts an HTTP server on ('', 8000), so it listens on every network interface, not just localhost. WebViewMeshRequestHandler.translate_path concatenates the raw request path without normalizing it or rejecting '..'. A raw HTTP request such as GET /mesh/../../../../etc/passwd (or a path outside the web root when the path does not start with /mesh) resolves to a file outside the mesh directory and is served. Any host on the local network can therefore read files the user can read while the viewer runs. The server is reachable through the installed meshviewer CLI executable; the GUI's serveWebViewer call is currently commented out.
findings.suggestion: Bind to 127.0.0.1, normalize with os.path.normpath/realpath and verify the result stays under the intended root (return 404 otherwise), or use SimpleHTTPRequestHandler's own translate_path logic. Document the server's exposure.

items.title: Committed __pycache__ .pyc files and a 16 MB test fixture are installed/carried

findings.title: Committed __pycache__ .pyc files and a 16 MB test fixture are installed/carried
findings.explanation: meshviewer/CMakeLists.txt copies the whole web_view_mesh directory into the install tree, so stale CPython-3.6 .pyc files ship to users; .gitignore only covers the root pattern. Auto3dgm/auto3dgm_nazar/tests/fixtures/test.ply (16 MB) and two 2 MB PNG textures are also committed rather than downloaded on demand.
findings.suggestion: Remove __pycache__ from the repository and exclude it from the install rule; move large fixtures to a download or a smaller sample.

items.title: Core alignment step requires the proprietary mosek solver under a separate academic license

findings.title: Core alignment step requires the proprietary mosek solver under a separate academic license
findings.evidence:
### specify mosek license
                file_path = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
                lic_path = os.path.join(file_path, '../lib/mosek.lic')
findings.explanation: The sparse assignment branch calls Mosek Fusion, which is commercial software; the module tells users to obtain an academic license (Auto3dgm.py:75). Academic mosek licenses are typically non-commercial, so users must be told the extension's core computation is not usable without a third-party license and is restricted to non-commercial use. Auto3dgm/auto3dgm_nazar/lib/Save_mosek_license_here is an empty placeholder, so no license is bundled (which is correct).
findings.suggestion: State the mosek dependency and its non-commercial academic restriction prominently in the module help and Readme.

items.title: Identity comparison against a string literal in subsample method dispatch

findings.title: Identity comparison against a string literal in subsample method dispatch
findings.explanation: `func is 'FPS'` relies on string interning; with a non-interned method string the function returns None and Job validation raises 'Unexpected value ... for type func'. The module currently passes method=None so it works by accident, but any caller supplying 'FPS' explicitly can break.
findings.suggestion: Use == for string comparison.

items.title: Module help text is the unmodified Slicer template and the registered test is empty

findings.title: Module help text is the unmodified Slicer template and the registered test is empty
findings.evidence:
self.parent.helpText = """
This is an example of scripted loadable module bundled in an extension.
It performs a simple thresholding on the input volume and optionally captures a screenshot.
"""
findings.explanation: Users opening the module see help text describing volume thresholding, which has nothing to do with the morphometrics workflow, and the acknowledgement credits the Slicer template authors. The ctest registered in Auto3dgm/CMakeLists.txt:32 runs Auto3dgmTest.test_Auto3dgm1, which is `pass` (Auto3dgm.py:928-929), so CI gives no signal about the pipeline.
findings.suggestion: Write real help text (inputs, parameters, outputs, mosek requirement, citation) and add at least a smoke test on the bundled fixtures.

items.title: No meaningful tests and minimal documentation

findings.title: No meaningful tests and minimal documentation
findings.evidence:
def test_Auto3dgm1(self):
      pass
findings.explanation: Auto3dgmTest.test_Auto3dgm1 is an empty pass, and the Testing/Python CMake registration is commented out. The module README is one line and the module help text still describes the template thresholding example. A user cannot verify the pipeline or learn the workflow from the extension.
findings.suggestion: Add a real test with the sample fixtures and a documented tutorial; update parent.helpText to describe Auto3dgm rather than the template.

items.title: No top-level license for the extension's Slicer glue code and meshviewer

findings.title: No top-level license for the extension's Slicer glue code and meshviewer
findings.evidence: <license/>
findings.explanation: The MIT license only covers the auto3dgm_nazar subpackage. The Auto3dgm module (Auto3dgm.py) and meshviewer have no license file or header, and the meshviewer.xml license element is empty. Distribution permission for the extension as a whole is therefore not explicit, although the core code is MIT.
findings.suggestion: Add a top-level LICENSE covering the Slicer module and meshviewer code, and fill in the meshviewer.xml license and contributor fields.

items.title: OFF parser ignores its argument and opens a hardcoded file

findings.title: OFF parser ignores its argument and opens a hardcoded file
findings.evidence:
def off_parser(file_path):
        file=open("hammas.off","r")
findings.explanation: Any .off mesh in the user's input folder is read from 'hammas.off' in the current working directory instead of the requested file, so .off inputs either fail with FileNotFoundError or silently analyse the wrong mesh. .off is in the accepted extension list (meshfactory.py:28), so this is reachable from the normal Load Data path.
findings.suggestion: Use open(file_path, 'r').

items.title: Output folder handling assumes a folder was chosen

findings.title: Output folder handling assumes a folder was chosen
findings.explanation: self.outputFolder starts as None and is only set by the folder dialog; the Run buttons are enabled by the input folder alone, so pressing Run without choosing an output folder raises TypeError on None + str instead of telling the user what is missing. Paths are also built by string concatenation rather than os.path.join.
findings.suggestion: Validate that an output folder is set and show a message; use os.path.join.

items.title: Process-wide MOSEKLM_LICENSE_FILE environment variable set at import of correspondence.py

findings.title: Process-wide MOSEKLM_LICENSE_FILE environment variable set at import of correspondence.py
findings.evidence:
file_path = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
os.environ.setdefault('MOSEKLM_LICENSE_FILE', os.path.join(file_path, '../lib/mosek.lic'))
findings.explanation: Importing this module mutates the Slicer process environment for all code that runs afterwards (including other extensions that might use mosek). It is imported lazily from Auto3dgmLogic.correspondence, so it does not fire at Slicer startup, but the side effect is global and silent.
findings.suggestion: Pass the license path explicitly to M.putlicensepath() (already done at line 468) and drop the environment mutation.

findings.title: Global environment variable set at import and mutation of stored alignment arrays
findings.evidence: os.environ.setdefault('MOSEKLM_LICENSE_FILE', os.path.join(file_path, '../lib/mosek.lic'))
findings.explanation: correspondence.py sets MOSEKLM_LICENSE_FILE in os.environ at import time for the whole Slicer process, which is a global side effect. exportRotations modifies the stored globalized rotation arrays in place (rot[2][0] = -1 * rot[2][0]), so calling the export twice changes results.
findings.suggestion: Pass the license path to the Mosek model only, avoid global env changes, and copy the rotation array before flipping its signs.

items.title: Test fixtures, a Windows-only binary and a 16 MB file are installed with the extension

findings.title: Test fixtures, a Windows-only binary and a 16 MB file are installed with the extension
findings.evidence:
install(DIRECTORY "auto3dgm_nazar"
  DESTINATION "${Slicer_INSTALL_QTSCRIPTEDMODULES_BIN_DIR}"
findings.explanation: CMake installs the whole auto3dgm_nazar directory, which contains tests/fixtures/test.ply (16 MB), a Windows-only compiled module lap_windows/_lapjv.cp36-win_amd64.pyd (not built by the CMake build and not loadable on Linux/macOS), and lap_windows/tests that import a 'lap' module that is not packaged. This bloats the package and ships an unused, platform-specific binary. The lap_windows package is not imported by the module code I read.
findings.suggestion: Install only the Python sources needed at runtime (or exclude tests/ and lap_windows/ with PATTERN filters) and move large fixtures out of the installed tree.

items.title: Transform export writes the wrong translation component

findings.title: Transform export writes the wrong translation component
findings.explanation: The third translation value is m[1,3] instead of m[2,3], so .tfm files written by saveTFM contain a wrong z translation. saveTFM is currently only reachable from dead/commented code paths, hence minor, but the exported transform would be silently incorrect if re-enabled.
findings.suggestion: Write str(m[2,3]) as the third component.

items.title: requirements.txt lists bare 'vtk', which would shadow Slicer's bundled VTK

findings.title: requirements.txt lists bare 'vtk', which would shadow Slicer's bundled VTK
findings.evidence:
numpy
vtk
findings.explanation: Nothing in the build or code reads this file, so it is not executed automatically; but a user or packager following it would pip-install a second VTK into Slicer's environment, which is a known way to break Slicer and other extensions. numpy is likewise bundled by Slicer.
findings.suggestion: Remove the file or replace it with a comment stating that numpy/VTK come from Slicer.

findings.title: requirements.txt lists 'vtk' and 'numpy', which could replace Slicer's bundled packages if installed
findings.evidence:
numpy
vtk
findings.explanation: The pip package vtk bundles its own VTK, which conflicts with Slicer's VTK if a user installs the requirements into Slicer's Python environment. The file is not installed automatically by the code I read, so the risk depends on users following it manually.
findings.suggestion: Remove vtk and numpy from requirements.txt (Slicer provides both) or document that it should not be installed into Slicer's Python.

items.title: Debug and dead-code leftovers in the shipped package

findings.title: Debug and dead-code leftovers in the shipped package
findings.evidence: import pdb
findings.explanation: pdb is imported at module import, and Auto3dgm/auto3dgm_nazar/analysis/mini-auto3dgm_barakshan.py executes matplotlib plotting code at import (it is not importable due to the dashes in its name, so it is dead weight). meshviewer/web_view_mesh/examples/http_server_two_dirs.py hardcodes '/Users/jmw110/data/bunny'. None of these affect users directly but they add noise to the installed package.
findings.suggestion: Remove debug imports, the scratch script, and the example file from the installed tree.
